Declare observed counts for an allocation model

Source: R/08-spax_obs.R
obs_flows.Rd

obs_flows() declares observed origin-facility counts and obs_totals() observed facility counts, in total or by demand group. Each returns a spax_obs: the counts together with the loss used to fit to them (and its arguments). The loss is part of the observation, so a model specification carries none. An observation holds no data. spax() aligns the observations with the data: it matches the IDs, reorders the counts into the order of the data and drops or refuses what the data cannot hold.

Usage

obs_flows(
  x,
  origin = NULL,
  facility = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  loss = c("poisson", "weighted_sse"),
  loss_args = list(),
  outside = "unknown"
)

obs_totals(
  x,
  facility = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  loss = c("poisson", "weighted_sse"),
  loss_args = list(),
  outside = "unknown"
)

# S3 method for class 'spax_obs'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

For obs_flows(), a numeric matrix of origin by facility counts or a data frame of origin, facility and count. For obs_totals(), a named numeric vector (or one-dimensional array or table) of facility counts, a facility by group matrix, or a data frame of facility and count, or of facility, group and count. For the print() method, a spax_obs.

origin, facility, count, group

Names of the columns of a data frame x holding the origin IDs, facility IDs, counts and group IDs. Leave all NULL to read the columns by position (see Details). They apply to data frames only.

loss

"poisson" (default) or "weighted_sse": the loss that fits a model to these counts.

loss_args

A named list of arguments for the loss. It is stored and passed on unchanged.

outside

The observed outside counts (see Details). For obs_flows(): "unknown" (the default), "known" (each origin's demand minus its counts at the facilities of the data) or a numeric vector named by origin ID. For obs_totals(): "unknown", one number (facility totals) or a numeric vector named by group ID (totals by group). Used with the Poisson loss only, and by a model with an outside option (spec_clm()).

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class spax_obs: a list with type ("flow", "utilization" or "utilization_by_group", the kind of counts), x (a double matrix, a named double vector, or for flows given as a data frame, a frame with columns origin, facility and count), loss, loss_args and outside ("unknown", "known", or the given outside counts). With outside counts, spax() compares the model with the output "flow_outside", "utilization_outside" or "utilization_outside_by_group" instead of type (see fit_allocation()).

Details

IDs. IDs from data frames are converted to character: factors with as.character(), numbers with format(scientific = FALSE), so that 100000 stays "100000" rather than "1e+05". Dimnames and names are used as given.

Counts are finite and nonnegative, or NA for a count that was not observed (an NA cell is left out of the loss). Fractional counts are allowed.

Flows. x is a numeric matrix with row names (origin IDs) and column names (facility IDs), or a data frame with one row per origin-facility pair. A table or xtabs object is read as a matrix. A frame with exactly three columns and no column arguments is read as origin, facility, count; otherwise name the columns. In a long table a pair that does not appear has count 0; duplicate pairs are summed, ignoring NA, and a pair whose counts are all NA stays NA.

Totals. x is a named numeric vector, a one-dimensional array or table (from tapply() or table()), or a data frame of facility and count (two columns by default). These are facility totals. A matrix with facility row names and group column names, or a data frame of facility, group and count (three columns by default), gives totals by demand group. Duplicate facilities in a frame are summed as for flows; duplicate names in a vector or matrix are an error. tapply() over a factor with unused levels gives NA for those facilities, which reads as unobserved, not as 0: use table(), or replace the NA by 0 if the facility had no counts.

What the data decides. When the observations are aligned with the data: counts from origins outside the data, excluded from it or with unknown demand are dropped with a message. For flows, counts at facilities outside the data are the outside option of the model (dropped, with a message, for a model without one). For totals, counts at facilities outside the data never enter the fit and are left out, with a message: there is no origin to send them to. Positive counts from origins with zero demand, at facilities with zero supply, on pairs with unknown or infinite travel, or (for totals) at facilities that no origin can reach are errors, because the model cannot produce them. Flows missing for an active origin or a facility of the data are taken as 0, with a message; totals must give every facility of the data (use 0, or NA if unobserved).

IDs match the data as text. An ID that matches nothing is then matched by its numeric value when exactly one ID of the data has that value, with a message: R writes the number 100000 as "1e+05", and codes read as numbers lose leading zeros (1234 matches "01234").

Outside counts. The outside option of a conditional logit model (spec_clm()) takes the demand of the active origins that goes to facilities outside the data or to none. By default (outside = "unknown") a fit uses the counts at the facilities of the data only. outside declares the observed counts of the outside option, which then become one more cell per origin of a flow fit (one more element of the totals, one more row of the totals by group) and are fitted with the Poisson loss, so outside is refused with another loss. A model without an outside option (spec_huff(), or spec_clm() with outside = 0) cannot carry them: spax() refuses the combination.

  • obs_flows(outside = "known") takes the outside count of an origin to be its demand minus its counts at the facilities of the data, y0 = D - sum(y). Counts of the origin at facilities outside the data are part of y0. It is computed for an active origin that appears in the observations and has no NA count at the facilities of the data. Any other active origin has an unknown outside count (NA) and is fitted on its facility counts alone, as without outside counts. Counts that exceed the demand of an origin by more than 1e-8 of it are an error; a smaller excess is set to 0.

  • obs_flows(outside = y0), with y0 a numeric vector named by origin ID, gives the outside counts: each name an active origin of the data once (the names of origins of the data that are not active are dropped with a message, any other name is an error), values nonnegative or NA. An active origin that is not named has an unknown outside count.

  • obs_totals(outside = y0) gives the outside count of facility totals as one number, and of totals by group as a numeric vector named by group ID (all groups of the data, NA for an unknown one). It is never derived from the totals: it is the demand of the data's active origins that went to facilities outside the data or to none. Totals often include people from outside the data (list sizes, for instance), and a difference would be biased.

Declare outside counts as known only when the demand counts the same people as the observations, for example registrations by residence from the same extract and date, where every resident is registered somewhere. They are not a population estimate: list sizes and population differ by several percent, and the gap goes straight into the outside count.

For an origin whose outside count is known and adds up, with its facility counts, to its demand (y0 + sum(y) = D, as for "known"), the Poisson loss on its cells is the multinomial likelihood of its choices up to constants. When this holds for every origin of an ungrouped flow fit and v0 is fitted inside its search bounds, the fitted total outside count equals the observed one. That is not claimed for totals or for demand groups: there the total outside count is not guaranteed to match. Fits with and without outside counts are fits to different data, so compare_allocations() gives no loss difference between them: compare models on the same observation, and compare the Huff model (spec_huff()) with a conditional logit model on an observation with outside = "unknown".

See also

Other allocation interface: decay_gaussian(), prep_data(), spax(), spax_access_values-methods, spax_allocation-methods, spax_huff(), spec_clm()

Examples

# Origin-facility flows from a long table of registrations
flows <- obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice",
                   count = "patients")
flows
#> <spax obs> flows: 3,188 origin-facility counts, total 601,269; loss poisson

# Facility totals, from the same table
totals <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$practice, sum)
obs_totals(totals)
#> <spax obs> totals: 55 facility counts, total 601,269; loss poisson

# The same flows with the outside counts known: demand counts the residents
# registered somewhere, so each origin's outside count is its demand minus
# its counts at the facilities of the data (used by a model with an outside
# option, see spax())
obs_flows(cornwall_flows, origin = "lsoa", facility = "practice",
          count = "patients", outside = "known")
#> <spax obs> flows: 3,188 origin-facility counts, total 601,269; loss poisson; outside counts known
